mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strengthening residential construction activity that precedes higher consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 1% month-over-month, or the rank correlation between HOUST and SPX returns falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 9.0% and remains below this threshold for two consecutive months, it signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and corporate hiring, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (UNRATE < 9.0% for two consecutive months), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the overall average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance in response to inflationary pressures, which supports equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 9.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals a labor market recovery that accelerates consumer spending and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 9.0%, a decline in UNRATE does not lead to positive 60-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the overall average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an easing monetary policy that reduces borrowing costs and stimulates economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX returns falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 650,000 units per month, it signals strong residential construction activity that precedes increased consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered instances (HOUST > 650.0), or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the overall average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand across multiple sectors, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST rise and RSAFS rise) fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a low industrial production regime (INDPRO < 95.0), a rebound in industrial output (INDPRO > 95.0) signals a recovery in manufacturing and supply chain activity that supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 95.0, a rebound to INDPRO > 95.0 does not lead to positive 60-day forward returns in more than 55% of cases, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) compared to the overall average.
